Radius / Pay4Me

I designed Pay4Me, now Radius, around education payments that matter to students and their families. I wanted the experience to make the recipient, currency, verification status and next step clear before money moves.

01What I wanted to solve

The person paying is not always the person studying abroad. I worked on sponsored payments, transaction tracking, verification and support, alongside the website that introduces the service.

02The decisions that mattered

Design for the person supporting the student.

I made sponsored payment a clear journey rather than treating every transfer as a payment to yourself.

Keep important context close to the money.

I placed currency controls with the balance and verification status beside the account identity.

Make help easy to reach.

I kept support in the main navigation and used recognisable education-payment terms on the website.

04What I can show, and what I would test

Evidence available. Radius is a live payments product. The linked website and mobile listings show the service; product traction is separate from evidence of my individual design impact.

Next validation. I would test a first sponsored payment and whether families understand the fees, timing and support options before sending money.

Radius is a live product with public app-store listings. Its traction is company-level evidence, not proof that my design caused it. I would test a first sponsored payment and check whether families understand the fees and timing.
